title: 48 Swahili Phrases in 11 Minutes | Learn Swahili for Beginners (Hobbies & Free Time)
description:
Learn 48 essential Swahili phrases in 11 minutes - the fun, fast way.
#Swahili #LearnSwahili #LanguageLearning

Every phrase follows the same rhythm: hear it in English, hear it in Kiswahili, then say it out loud with the pronunciation guide. Perfect for beginners, travellers and anyone who wants to speak Swahili with confidence.

WHAT YOU GET
- 8 themed chapters, 48 real-life phrases
- Kiswahili audio from a native voice
- English pronunciation guide for every line
- A brand-new lesson every single day

CHAPTERS
0:07  Hobbies & Free Time · Mambo ya Kufanya na Wakati wa Upole
1:24  Patience · Subira
2:38  Hotel & Accommodation · Hoteli na Malazi
3:52  Weather & Small Talk · Hali ya Hewa na Mazungumzo Madogo
5:10  Ordering Food & Dining · Kuagiza Chakula na Kulia
6:25  Growth · Ukuaji
7:57  Sports & Fitness · Michezo na Mazoezi
9:16  Confidence · Kujiamini

PHRASE LIST

HOBBIES & FREE TIME · Mambo ya Kufanya na Wakati wa Upole
• I love walking after work. - Naipenda kutembea baada ya kazi.  [Naipenda kutembea baadA ya kazi.]
• I journal when the day slows. - Ninaandika jarida siku ikilegea.  [Ninaandika jARIda siku ikileGEA.]
• I water plants and feel better. - Naweka maji kwenye mimea, napata nafuu.  [Naweka maji kwenye MImea, napata nAFuu.]
• Cooking dinner gives me comfort. - Kupika chakula cha jioni hunipa faraja.  [Kupika chakula cha jioni hunipa FARaja.]
• I do yoga, just ten minutes. - Nafanya yoga, dakika kumi tu.  [Nafanya YOga, dakika KUmi tu.]
• I try a new recipe sometimes. - Mara nyingine najaribu mapishi mapya.  [Mara nyingine naJARibu maPISHI maPya.]

PATIENCE · Subira
• I can breathe, then wait. - Naweza kupumua, kisha subiri.  [Na-we-za pu-mu-a, ki-kha su-bi-ri.]
• Wait without judging yourself. - Subiri bila kujihukumu.  [Su-bi-ri bi-la ku-ji-hu-ku-mu.]
• Good things take real time. - Mambo mazuri huchukua muda.  [Ma-am-bo ma-zu-ri hu-chi-ku-a mu-da.]
• I choose calm over quick reactions. - Ninachagua utulivu kuliko majibu ya haraka.  [Ni-na-chi-a-gu-a u-tu-li-vu ku-liko ma-ji-bu ya ha-ra-ka.]
• Let your body catch up. - Mwili wako nao ufuate polepole.  [Mwi-li wa-ko nao u-fu-a-te po-le-po-le.]
• No rush, just steady steps. - Hakuna kukimbilia, hatua kwa hatua tu.  [Ha-ku-na ku-ki-mbi-lli-a, ha-tua kwa ha-tua tu.]

HOTEL & ACCOMMODATION · Hoteli na Malazi
• Can I get an extra key? - Naomba ufunguo wa ziada, tafadhali.  [Naomba U-FUN-KU-O wa ZI-A-da, ta-faDHA-li.]
• Is breakfast included in my rate? - Je, kifungua kinywa kimejumuishwa kwenye bei?  [Je, ki-FU-riA-ngua ki-NYWA ki-me-JUMU-shi-wa kwen-gE-ni bEi?]
• What time is check-out tomorrow? - Kesho muda wa kuondoka ni saa ngapi?  [KE-sho MU-da wa ku-ON-do-ka ni Saa NGA-pi?]
• Could I switch rooms, please? - Naweza kubadilisha chumba, tafadhali?  [Na-weza ku-BA-DI-li-sha CHUM-ba, ta-faDHA-li?]
• Is there parking on site? - Maegesho yapo hapa kwenye eneo?  [MA-e-GE-sho ya-po HA-pa kwen-gE-ni E-ne-o?]
• Do you have a quiet room option? - Mna chumba chenye utulivu zaidi?  [M-na CHUM-ba CHEN-ye u-tu-LI-vi za-i-di?]

WEATHER & SMALL TALK · Hali ya Hewa na Mazungumzo Madogo
• The rain just started, finally. - Mvua imeanza tu, hatimaye.  [M-VU-a i-me-an-za tu, ha-ti-ma-ye.]
• Do you feel that cool breeze? - Unahisi upepo wa baridi namna hii?  [U-na-hisi u-pe-po wa ba-ri-di nam-na hi-i?]
• It might drizzle later, are you ready? - Inaweza kunyanyuka kidogo baadaye, uko tayari?  [I-na-weza ku-nyan-yu-ka ki-do-go baa-da-ye, u-ko ta-ya-ri?]
• My windows fogged up already. - Madirisha yameanza kupazuka ukungu.  [Ma-di-ri-sha ya-me-an-za ku-pa-zu-ka ukun-gu.]
• The sky is bright, no worries. - Anga ni angavu, hakuna hofu.  [An-ga ni an-ga-vu, ha-ku-na ho-fu.]
• Wow, the sun is warm today. - Polepole, jua leo linapasha moto.  [Po-le-po-le, ju-a le-o lin-a-pa-sha mo-to.]

ORDERING FOOD & DINING · Kuagiza Chakula na Kulia
• What comes with this meal? - NiNini kinakuja na chakula hiki?  [Ni-NI-ni ki-na-ku-ja na cha-ku-la hi-chi?]
• Can I see the menu, please? - Naomba nione menyu, tafadhali.  [Na-OMba ni-o-ne me-nyu, ta-fa-dha-li.]
• Is this dish freshly made today? - Sahani hii imetayarishwa leo, hivi punde?  [Sa-ha-ni hi-ii i-me-ta-ya-ri-shwa le-o, hi-vi pun-de?]
• I want it less oily, please. - Ningependa kiwe si chenye mafuta mengi.  [Nin-ge-pen-da ki-we si ch-EN-ye ma-fa-ta mengi.]
• Can you make it vegetarian for me? - Naomba kiwe cha mboga tu, inawezekana?  [Na-OMba ki-we cha mBO-ga tu, i-na-we-zeka-na?]
• I’ll take the chef’s special, please. - Naomba nipate maalum ya mpishi.  [Na-OMba ni-pa-te ma-a-lum ya m-pi-shi.]

GROWTH · Ukuaji
• I start small, and I follow through. - Naanza kidogo, na naendelea hadi mwisho.  [Naanza KIDOGO, na NAENDELEA hadi MWISHO.]
• I practice daily, even when it feels messy. - Nafanya mazoezi kila siku, hata yakichanganya moyo.  [Nafanya MAZOEZI kila SIKU, hata yakichanganya MOYO.]
